sections.label: Dockless vehicle-sharing licensing regime
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a licensing regime for dockless vehicle-sharing operators covering bicycles, PMDs and PABs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, the Bill introduces a licensing regime for dockless vehicle-sharing operators, which will cover sharing services for bicycles, PMDs and PABs.

sections.label: Parking provision in private developments
sections.summary: The Bill allows the Government to improve management of parking provision by private developments to support the car-lite vision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill will allow the Government to improve the management of parking provision by private developments to support our car-lite vision.

sections.label: Growth of dockless bicycle-sharing
sections.summary: Dockless bicycle-sharing started just over a year ago, expanded rapidly, and there are now more than 100,000 shared bicycles in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Dockless bicycle-sharing started just over a year ago and has expanded rapidly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: There are now more than 100,000 shared bicycles in Singapore.

sections.label: LTA removal notices and fines
sections.summary: Since mid-last year, LTA issued more than 2,100 removal notices and collected about $180,000 in fines and administrative fees from operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Since mid-last year, LTA has issued more than 2,100 removal notices and collected about $180,000 in fines and administrative fees from the operators.

sections.label: Managing operator fleet size
sections.summary: LTA will manage each operator's fleet size using section 8G powers to impose licensing conditions, including maximum fleet size.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, LTA will manage the size of each operator’s fleet.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This will be done by using its powers under section 8G to impose licensing conditions, including conditions on the maximum fleet size that each operator can deploy.

sections.label: Regulatory action and improper parking bans
sections.summary: Regulatory action ranges from reducing fleet size to financial penalties, suspension or cancellation, and LTA will direct operators to collectively ban individuals who persistently park improperly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Regulatory action ranges from reducing the maximum fleet size, imposing financial penalties of up to $100,000 for each instance of non-compliance, suspending or even cancelling licences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Third, LTA will direct licensed operators to work together to collectively ban individuals who persistently park improperly in public places.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This means that an individual who has been found to have parked improperly at least three times in a calendar year when renting from one or more operators, will be banned temporarily from renting from all operators.

sections.label: Penalty on conviction
sections.summary: Conviction carries a fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The penalty, on conviction, is a fine of up to $10,000, or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

sections.label: LTA parking approval and charges
sections.summary: LTA may administratively approve parking provisions, and the Bill empowers LTA and HDB and URA officers to prescribe parking charges and decide on detained vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Alternatively, LTA can administratively approve parking provisions, taking into consideration factors, such as the proximity to the development of public transport facilities, or the availability of other parking places in the vicinity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This will allow developers to trial new concepts of space and land planning, and new parking concepts, such as hub car parks in future car-lite precincts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Today, the PPA requires the Minister for Transport to prescribe parking charges for HDB and URA's car parks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We are, hence, amending the PPA to empower the LTA Superintendent and HDB’s and URA’s Deputy and Assistant Superintendents to prescribe parking charges for HDB and URA car parks, via clause 7 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In view of the volume of decisions to detain vehicles found abandoned or parked unlawfully, and to improve operational efficiency, clause 11 amends section 15 to allow the Superintendent as well as authorised officers to also make these decisions on his behalf.

sections.label: Licensing bike sharing operators
sections.summary: Clause 6 will license all bike sharing operators in Singapore, which is strongly supported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In particular, we strongly support clause 6 which will license all bike sharing operators in Singapore.

sections.label: Cycling path width
sections.summary: Cycling paths should preferably be about 3.5 metres wide so novice and experienced cyclists can cycle safely.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In addition, cycling paths should be wide enough, preferably about 3.5 metres in width, so that both novice and experienced cyclists can cycle safely.

sections.label: Demerit points and accident liability
sections.summary: The Bill sets performance standards, and the speaker urges a demerit point penalty system and default liability on cyclists and PMD users for footpath accidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Bill has specified performance standards for the licensee.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: However, it will be more effective if LTA can introduce a penalty system which imposes demerit points on the licensee, based on different types of infringements, eventually culminating in the termination of operating licences upon reaching a certain threshold.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to consider imposing default liability on cyclists and PMD users if an accident occurs along a pedestrian footpath, unless it is proven that the accident is attributed to the behaviour of pedestrians, rather than the cyclists and PMD users.

sections.label: Moving towards car-lite society
sections.summary: The amendment to the Bill intends to move Singapore towards a car-lite society.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment to the Bill has, with it, the intention to move Singapore towards a car-lite society.

sections.label: Fines for indiscriminately parked bicycles
sections.summary: Penalties including fines of up to $100,000 for operators who did not remove indiscriminately parked bicycles require behavioural change.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Penalties, including hefty fines of up to $100,000 for operators who did not manage to remove indiscriminately parked bicycles, require behavioural change.

sections.label: Extending penalty assistance to operators
sections.summary: A question asks whether LTA will extend assistance or exemption of penalty to operators who perform due diligence to incentivise correct user behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will LTA be open to extending assistance/exemption of penalty for the operators who perform the necessary due diligence to incentivise correct behaviour among users?

sections.label: Definition of near train stations
sections.summary: A question asks for the definition of "near" regarding reduction in car park spaces for new developments near train stations.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On reduction in car park spaces for new developments near train stations, what is the definition of "near"?

sections.label: Licensing regime and geofencing solution
sections.summary: Under the proposed amendments, LTA will introduce a licensing regime, limit operator maximum fleet size and implement a QR code-enabled geofencing solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, LTA will be introducing a licensing regime, limiting operator’s maximum fleet size and implementing a QR code-enabled geofencing solution.

sections.label: Banning errant users from device-sharing
sections.summary: The Bill lets LTA ask operators to collectively ban errant users for a period, and a Member hopes LTA will consider fining banned users caught riding with someone else's identity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): The Bill has a provision whereby LTA can ask operators to collectively ban errant users who failed to park responsibly, for a period of time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: LTA's aim is to ensure that recalcitrant users will not be able to use any device-sharing services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope LTA would consider tightening this rule further by imposing a fine on the errant users if they are caught riding using someone else’s identity, while under a ban.

sections.label: CBD office building car park requirement
sections.summary: The car park requirement in a Central Business District office building is 0.2 parking lots per 100 square metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The car park requirement in a Central Business District (CBD) office building is 0.2 parking lots per 100 square metres (m2).

sections.label: CBD season parking fee survey
sections.summary: A 2011 Colliers International survey showed Singapore's median CBD season parking fee was $278 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A Colliers International survey done in 2011 showed that Singapore's median season parking fee in the CBD was $278 per month.

sections.label: Yellow boxes and parking places
sections.summary: The speaker supports LTA's plan for more yellow boxes but questions whether 50,000 additional parking places in two years suffice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I support LTA’s plan to designate more yellow boxes at HDB void decks, MRT stations and bus stops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, I wonder whether the planned additional 50,000 parking places within the next two years are enough.

sections.label: Bike-sharing companies sharing costs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests bike-sharing companies share costs, even a symbolic $1 per month per site, to encourage co-responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To encourage co-responsibility, I suggest the bike-sharing companies be made to share the costs, even if it is a symbolic $1 per month per site.

sections.label: Temporary ban for irresponsible parking
sections.summary: The speaker calls it an air, sea, land problem and supports a temporary ban on users who repeatedly park bicycles irresponsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, this is really an "air, sea, land" problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the provision that all operators will impose a temporary ban on users who repeatedly park the bicycles irresponsibly.

sections.label: Licensing operators and bicycle usage study
sections.summary: The amendments require operators to apply for a licence, and a study of 10,000 bikes found each rented 30 minutes daily on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments require that all operators must apply for a licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will help the Government to control the quality of the operators and ensure that they properly manage the number of bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is estimated that out of the 100,000 bicycles, only half are frequently used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recently, the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) and the Singapore Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Alliance for Research and Technology did a study on one major bike-sharing operator in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They analysed their data of 10,000 bikes in April and May 2017 and found that each bike was only rented for 30 minutes a day on average.

sections.label: Questions on private owners and hirer responsibility
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether provisions apply only to shared vehicle operators and users, and how hirers will shoulder equal responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Personally, I have also had to manoeuvre through obstacle courses made up of indiscriminately parked bicycles at the void decks, including those at my own block.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I wish to clarify if these provisions and restrictions apply only to vehicle hiring operators and users or hirers of shared vehicles, such as bicycles or PMDs, and not to private owners of similar vehicles?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Are there plans to require private bicycle or PMD owners to be registered so that proper monitoring of indiscriminate parking and subsequent enforcement can be carried out?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, while the amendments in this Bill seek to rein in on the licensing requirements of the operators of shared vehicles in order to bring about greater responsibility towards the hiring of shared vehicles, how will the users or hirers of such shared vehicles also be made to shoulder equal responsibility in the use and parking of these shared vehicles?

sections.label: Interim parking for dispatch riders
sections.summary: LTA is asked to work with private developments to provide free interim parking lots for dispatch riders and food deliverers for 10 to 15 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can LTA work with the management of such private developments to provide designated Interim Parking Lots for dispatch riders and food deliverers to park their motorcycles or PMDs for free for a period of no more than 10 to 15 minutes so that they would not get parking offence summonses and would not obstruct traffic or pedestrian access?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: First, Mr Gan Thiam Poh expressed his support for LTA's management of the size of each operator's fleet by setting a maximum fleet size.

sections.label: Penalty framework for licensees
sections.summary: LTA will look into the penalty framework for licensees and take strong action against repeated or serious infringements, including licence revocation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to Dr Teo Ho Pin’s suggestion on the penalty framework for licensees, we will look into it as LTA works out the implementation details of the licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We would also like to assure Dr Teo Ho Pin and Dr Intan Mokhtar that LTA will take strong action against repeated or serious infringements of licence requirements, including revocation of the operator's licence.

sections.label: Bicycle parking spaces added
sections.summary: Fifty thousand bicycle parking spaces will be added by 2020 at MRT stations, HDB estates and parks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Fifty thousand bicycle parking spaces will be added by 2020 at MRT stations, HDB estates and parks.

sections.label: QR code parking verification
sections.summary: Each parking location will have a unique QR code, and users may only end their trip if the scanned code matches the parking location's GPS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Each parking location will have a unique QR code and users will only be allowed to end their trip if the scanned QR code matches the GPS location of the parking location.

sections.label: Collective ban and parking requirement
sections.summary: Firmer steps, including a collective ban, will deter irresponsible behaviour, and users cannot end trips until bicycles are parked in designated areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Hence, it is necessary to take firmer steps to deter irresponsible user behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We will do so through the collective ban.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Users will also not be allowed to end their trips with the operators until the bicycles are parked within designated parking areas.

sections.label: Regulatory sandbox for new operators
sections.summary: A regulatory sandbox is being considered for new operators, granting a smaller fleet and a subset of full licence requirements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To reduce barriers to entry for new operators and encourage innovation, we are considering implementing a "regulatory sandbox" for new operators with no track record.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We recognise that new operators could benefit from a trial phase as they scale up their operations and learn how to manage their fleet responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: They would be granted a much smaller fleet and subjected to a subset of the full licence requirements.

sections.label: Bicycle-sharing MOU and licensing
sections.summary: Maintenance and liability are covered under the MOU, operators have purchased insurance, and the licensing regime covers dockless vehicle-sharing operators, not privately owned vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Maintenance standards and liability issues are covered under the MOU with the operators and all bicycle-sharing operators under the MOU have purchased insurance for riders and third parties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: With regard to Dr Intan Mokhtar's query, the licensing regime is for dockless vehicle-sharing operators and will not cover privately owned vehicles and devices.

sections.label: New parking standards implementation
sections.summary: The new parking standards will apply only to new developments and existing developments undergoing redevelopment and major Additions and Alteration works.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked a few questions about how we will implement the new parking standards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This will apply only to new developments as well as existing developments undergoing redevelopment and major Additions and Alteration (A&A) works.

sections.label: LTA parking provision tools
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments give LTA a wider range of tools to better calibrate parking provision requirements for private developments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The amendments in the Bill will give LTA a wider range of tools to better calibrate parking provision requirements for private developments.

sections.label: Drawing yellow boxes
sections.summary: We will try to draw yellow boxes as near to the place of residence as possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As much as possible, we will try to draw yellow boxes as near to the place of residence as possible.

sections.label: Parking amendments and public notice
sections.summary: The amendments clarify LTA's waiver power, replace "public land" with "public place", and clarify how HDB and URA give public notice of parking charges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The amendments make clear that LTA's power to waive parking provision requirements pertains to requirements that are stated in the rules made under the new section 22.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The amendment replaces a reference to "public land" in the new section 8P with "public place", which is the specific term that is defined and used in the new Part 3.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The amendments clarify ways that HDB and URA can give public notice, when fixing or changing parking charges at their car parks, by publishing these rates in newspapers, publishing the charges on HDB or URA's websites, or in any other way that would secure adequate publicity.
